news.title: Tuchel should listen to ‘the 0.1%’ to learn from England’s World Cup mistakes | Jacob Steinberg
news.lede: Head coach is keen to focus on positives but Nations League squad hints at desire for greater tactical options. Thomas Tuchel should be listening to the 0.1%. As Tuchel unveiled his first England squad since the World Cup, he said 99.9% of supporters he bumped into did not talk about his substitutions during the Argentina game. According to him, the conversation is far more positive.

news.title: Hans-Joachim Watzke reveals that he considered making Thomas Tuchel Germany coach after 2022 World Cup
news.lede: It seems Germany could have had a change in coach sooner after the 2022 FIFA World Cup. Hans-Joachim Watzke, vice-president of the German Football Association (DFB), revealed to Sky Sport (as captured by @iMiaSanMia) that after Germany’s group stage exit in Qatar, he had considered replacing then-national coach Hansi Flick with Thomas Tuchel. Tuchel was without a job at the time after being sacked by Chelsea. We were knocked out quite miserably in Qatar.

news.title: Mbappe leaves Nike, signs with On as it enters football
news.lede: Kylian Mbappe remained a centrepiece of Nike's football marketing at this year's Fifa World Cup, most recently receiving signature editions of its Mercurial boots. (EPA Images pic) PARIS: French soccer star Kylian Mbappe has ended his two-decade-long partnership with Nike and signed with Swiss sportswear brand On, the latest blow for the American brand as newer rivals gain ground in the athletic footwear market. On plans to launch its first football boots in 2027, and also named former French player Thierry Henry as its director of football. On's US-listed shares were up 5% in premarket trading.

news.title: Thomas Tuchel: England fans don't ask me about my substitutions against Argentina in the World Cup semi-final
news.lede: Thomas Tuchel says "99.9 per cent" of England fans do not talk about substitutions or tactical decisions when reflecting on their World Cup experience. Tuchel faced intense scrutiny over his decision-making during England's 2-1 semi-final defeat by Argentina, but the Three Lions boss says supporters focus on other things when reflecting on the tournament. England took the lead through Anthony Gordon in the second half, but Enzo Fernandez struck late on before Lautaro Martinez completed Argentina's comeback.
